newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Tourist arrivals to Singapore rise 2.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Tourist arrivals to Singapore rise 2.4 percent.

text.p: The number of tourists visiting Singapore rose 2.4 percent to 4.87 million in the first eight months of 1996, the Singapore Tourist Promotion Board (STPB) said on Friday.
However, visitor arrivals fell 4.8 percent in August over the same month last year, due partly to a decline in arrivals from some Asian countries, the STPB said in a statement.

It said a switch in Japanese traffic to Hong Kong before its handover to China in 1997 and cancellations by Taiwanese travellers due to concerns over health conditions in Southeast Asia contributed to the decline.
"We will continue to monitor the performance of these markets closely," Tan Chin Nam, chief executive of the STPB, said in the statement.

Arrivals from the United States in the first eight months increased 10.3 percent, while the number of visitors from South Korea rose 12.8 percent. Visitors from China and India rose 17 percent and 10.2 percent respectively.
